UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user profile on the Virasya platform, encompassing both artisans (sellers) and buyers (craft enthusiasts). This entity stores core user information and their assigned role.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

name.description: The full name of the user.

email.description: The email address of the user, used for communication and login.

role.description: The role of the user within the platform, determining their access and functionalities. It can be 'artisan' or 'buyer'.

location.description: The geographical location of the user (e.g., city, state, country).

preferredLanguage.description: The user's preferred language for interacting with the platform's UI and content (e.g., 'en' for English, 'hi' for Hindi).

profilePhotoUrl.description: The URL to the user's profile photo, typically stored in a cloud storage service like Firebase Storage.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents an authentic handcrafted product listed by an Artisan for display and sale on the Virasya marketplace. This entity includes product details, AI-generated content, and marketing information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

artisanId.description: Reference to the UserProfile of the artisan who owns and created this product listing. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Product)

name.description: The title or name of the product, often AI-generated for clarity and SEO.

description.description: A concise description of the product, highlighting its features and appeal, often AI-generated.

craftType.description: The primary category or type of the craft (e.g., Pottery, Textiles, Jewelry), often AI-detected from product images.

craftStyle.description: A more specific style or sub-category within the craft type (e.g., 'Khurja Pottery', 'Block Print Textiles'). This field can be AI-generated.

regionOfOrigin.description: The geographic region or place where the craft originated or is traditionally practiced.

materials.description: A detailed description of the materials used in crafting the product, often AI-identified.

laborHours.description: The estimated number of hours an artisan spent creating the product, a key input for AI price guidance.

complexity.description: The estimated complexity level of the craft, influencing AI price guidance (e.g., 'Low', 'Medium', 'High').

price.description: The final selling price of the product, set by the artisan after considering AI price suggestions.

imageUrl.description: An array of URLs to high-quality images of the product, stored in Firebase Storage.

story.description: A rich, narrative story about the craft, its cultural tradition, and the artisan, generated by AI based on structured facts.

tags.description: An array of SEO-friendly keywords and tags associated with the product to improve discoverability in searches and filters, often AI-generated.

status.description: The current publication status of the product listing (e.g., 'Draft' for unpublished, 'Published' for live on marketplace).

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the product listing was initially created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the product listing was modified.

instagramCaption.description: AI-generated caption text suitable for an Instagram marketing post, based on product details.

whatsAppMessage.description: AI-generated promotional message suitable for sharing via WhatsApp, based on product details.

marketingHashtags.description: AI-generated hashtags to accompany social media marketing posts, improving visibility.

BrowsingHistory.title: BrowsingHistory
BrowsingHistory.description: Captures a buyer's interactions with the marketplace, including viewed products and search queries, to inform personalized recommendations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the BrowsingHistory entry.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile of the buyer whose browsing history is being recorded. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N BrowsingHistory)

viewedProductIds.description: An array of IDs of products that the user has viewed.

searchQueries.description: An array of search terms or phrases entered by the user.

timestamp.description: Timestamp indicating the last time this browsing history entry was updated.

Recommendation.title: Recommendation
Recommendation.description: Stores AI-generated personalized product recommendations for specific buyers, facilitating discovery of relevant crafts.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Recommendation entry.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile of the buyer for whom these recommendations are generated. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Recommendation)

recommendedProductIds.description: An array of IDs of products recommended to the user.

generatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when these specific recommendations were generated.

Supports QAPs for both artisan-specific listings and public marketplace discovery.

params.name: productId
params.description: The unique identifier for the product listing.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for Virasya prioritizes secure, scalable, and debuggable access control by strictly adhering to the core design principles. 

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**

*   **For Products:** The `products` collection, despite serving both artisan drafts and public marketplace listings, achieves authorization independence. Each `Product` document contains an `artisanId` field. This denormalized field allows security rules to instantly verify ownership (`request.auth.uid == resource.data.artisanId`) without needing to perform a `get()` operation on a parent `UserProfile` document or any other collection. This is critical for robust atomic operations and simplified rule logic.

*   **For User-Specific Data (Browsing History, Recommendations):** Collections like `/users/{userId}/browsingHistory` and `/users/{userId}/recommendations` leverage path-based ownership. The `{userId}` wildcard in the path directly corresponds to `request.auth.uid`, making authorization checks trivial (`request.auth.uid == userId`). This eliminates the need for any denormalization *within* these subcollections, as the authorization context is already part of the document's location.

**Structural Segregation and QAPs (Queryable Authorization Patterns):**

*   **User Profiles (`/userProfiles/{userId}`):** This collection is designed for homogeneous security. Each document represents a user's profile, accessible primarily by the owner (`request.auth.uid == userId`). Rules can selectively allow public reads for `artisan` profiles based on their `role` field, creating clear segregation of access intent.

*   **Products (`/products/{productId}`):** This collection demonstrates effective segregation through a single `status` field (`Draft` or `Published`) within each document, rather than separate collections for drafts and published items. This simplifies data management and allows for powerful QAPs:
    *   **Artisan QAP:** To retrieve their own products (drafts or published), an artisan's query must include a filter for `artisanId == request.auth.uid`. The security rules will enforce `allow list: if request.auth.uid == request.query.where.artisanId;`, ensuring that artisans can only list *their own* products.
    *   **Buyer/Public Marketplace QAP:** To retrieve public products, a buyer's query must include `status == 'Published'`. The security rules will enforce `allow list: if resource.data.status == 'Published';`, ensuring only publicly available items are returned. This avoids rules acting as filters post-query, maintaining security and performance.

*   **User-Specific Subcollections (`/users/{userId}/browsingHistory`, `/users/{userId}/recommendations`):** These collections are inherently segregated, with each subcollection being entirely private to the `userId` specified in its path. QAPs are straightforward: `allow list: if request.auth.uid == userId;` ensures users can only list their own data.

This design leverages explicit state modeling (e.g., `status` field in Product), consistent naming conventions (e.g., `artisanId`, descriptive wildcards), and structural patterns to create a highly predictable, secure, and debuggable Firestore schema for Virasya.
